1. Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.

2. Model overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 38+), producing overly optimistic short-term forecasts that overshoot true values — cap forecast at 10–15% below the immediate prior peak.

3. Model fails to capture late-stage price surges (e.g., 40+ after 35+), often underestimating momentum — increase forecast by 5–10% for days 20–30 if prior 7-day average > 35.

4. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — over-predicts downward corrections after spikes — add a 2–3% upward bias to forecasts following a 35+ spike.

5. Model lags in recognizing true price direction — forecast often lags true trend by 2–4 days — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if true outcome shows accelerating upward trend.

6. Model underestimates volatility in late-stage price runs — increase forecast variance by 10–15% for days 25–30 if true outcome shows >5% daily movement.
